scope: All 14 numbered environments of Section 3 of diagonal-antidiagonal.tex. The review inspects the LaTeX statements and proofs and the Lean declarations and proofs, and modifies and compiles no LaTeX. It is a semantic source review, not a kernel build.
conventions: Lean names below include the BoxLike namespace. System is the contracting diagonal/anti-diagonal System structure; PlanarSystem is an arbitrary planar self-affine system and MatrixTuple an arbitrary tuple of real 2 x 2 matrices. Finite alphabets have the discrete measurable structure; invariant measures are Borel probability measures unless stated otherwise. No library axiom is used: listed literature inputs are explicit Prop-valued hypotheses.

proof_route_flags: 3.1 proves the box-like case of Oseledets' theorem through Birkhoff's theorem instead of citing it
3.3 proves the cited nested-disintegration results of Einsiedler-Ward
3.5 and 3.7 prove Feng's identity along his Lemmas 4.4 and 4.5, with the planar Oseledets theorem for mu(Sigma') = 1
3.6 follows Feng's (4.17) with the Shannon-McMillan-Breiman theorem, proved by Breiman's argument

3.10 proves existence variationally and ergodicity from uniqueness, and the Gibbs bounds and uniqueness for 0<s<2 from FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium through the rescaling and the one-sided reduction of the prose; the library proves FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium (fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_holds) by the quasi-multiplicativity of the norm, Bowen's construction with periodic-orbit measures and a bound on the relative entropy of the cylinder partitions; for box-like tuples with rotations, irreducible or not, it proves the whole proposition by a bound on the relative entropy of the cylinder partitions and the ergodicity of the image of Bowen's Gibbs measure
3.11 takes the uniqueness and ergodicity of mu^(2) from 3.10 for A^2, which has rotations, without the irreducibility of A^2
3.13 also has an integrated proof of the counting inequality without Birkhoff's theorem; neither proof uses proximality

3.14 is proved (fraserJordanJurgaDecomposition_holds) from Bowen's theorem with no literature premise; the Gibbs bounds of the equilibrium state are EquilibriumGibbsStatement, a theorem of the library (equilibriumGibbs)

primary_source_check.locations: Section 4, printed pp. 22-29: assumptions (4.1)-(4.7), partitions preceding Lemma 4.2, entropy definition (4.15), Lemma 4.6 (4.16)-(4.17), Corollary 4.7.
primary_source_check.assessment: Feng assumes an invariant Borel probability measure on the full two-sided finite shift and average contraction. Condition (4.7) fixes the number and multiplicities of Lyapunov exponents, without requiring ergodicity. The partitions fix the past and the projected point modulo the decreasing backward Oseledets filtration. Equation (4.16) gives the finite conditional-information sum and its Birkhoff limit; (4.17) separately gives the unconditional cylinder-mass limit using SMB. The Lean identities have the correct sign and forward-shift order. Strict contraction and planar ergodicity with simple spectrum suffice; the scalar nonergodic case has one exponent of multiplicity one, and extension by zero from Sigma_Z is valid. Feng's full-measure set also imposes forward-growth properties absent from Lean's past-defined SigmaPrime, so the atoms differ pointwise in general and the conditional measures agree almost everywhere (System.condMeas_fengXi_ae_eq). Corollary 4.7 states a global a.e. equivalence; Lean correctly derives the stronger pointwise equivalence from (4.16).

entries.label: thm:lyapunov_exponents_via_g_system
entries.fidelity: Statement: `MatrixTuple.OseledetsSet S.mat μ` is the article's choice of Σ′ and filtration ((V1)–(V3), Borel graph, σ(Σ′)=Σ′, μ(Σ′)=1, past-saturated); Σ^τ, Σ^ω are defined by V¹ being the y-axis and the x-axis. A choice exists (`System.oseledetsSet`, the Oseledets theorem for box-like tuples, proved through Birkhoff), and for every choice and every 𝐢 ∈ Σ′ the four limits hold (`System.lyapunov_exponents_via_g_system_manuscript`). The theorems of Oseledets and Froyland-Lloyd-Quas that the article cites are proved for box-like tuples. the hypotheses (proximal, rotations, ergodic, λ_2<λ_1) are those of the article; the four limits use only (V3), the case split uses λ_2<λ_1, existence uses ergodicity. The rate-defined `S.SigmaTau μ`, `S.SigmaOmega μ`, `S.xi μ i` used downstream are the article's objects for the box-like choice and agree modulo null sets with those of every choice (`sigmaTau_ae_eq`, `condMeas_oseledetsXi_ae_eq`); Feng's partitions of his admissible set have the same conditional measures almost everywhere (`condMeas_fengXi_ae_eq`). Gap: the Furstenberg measure Π_*μ is not formalised beyond the support of V¹ on the axes; measurability of subspaces is a Borel graph condition; Feng's admissible set is modelled through its atoms (any Borel full-measure set with the filtration of his (4.6)).
proof_deviations: Proof: as in the prose: (V3) and the matrix/projective derivative identity of `thm:matrix_products_g_derivatives`, with V¹ a coordinate axis (`V_one_eq_axis`).

entries.label: thm:conditional_measures_of_a_conditional_measure
entries.exact_hypotheses: Any standard Borel space Omega; probability measure mu; measurable partition xi; Borel Xi with positive mass. The saturated conclusion additionally assumes every atom through Xi lies in Xi.
entries.fidelity: Exact, and more general than either shift space. Equality of measures gives the simultaneous quantifier over all Borel A. Positivity holds mu_Xi-almost everywhere; the saturated identity holds mu-almost everywhere on Xi.

entries.label: thm:double_conditional
entries.exact_hypotheses: Any standard Borel Omega; probability measure mu; measurable partitions xi and xi'; pointwise refinement xi'(x) subset xi(x). Full-measure-domain partitions in the paper are represented by extension with one null atom.
entries.fidelity: Both the iterated conditional-measure identity and the iterated integral identity are proved. Lean writes nonnegative ENNReal integrals of measure evaluations; this is equivalent to the article's bounded nonnegative real integrals.
proof_deviations: The prose cites Einsiedler-Ward Proposition 5.20 and Theorem 5.14. Lean proves the needed nested-disintegration identities directly using conditional expectation, countable generating pi-systems and uniqueness. This is an expanded foundational proof, with no additional external premise.

entries.label: thm:finer_partition_dirac_mass
entries.exact_hypotheses: Standard Borel Omega; probability measure; two measurable partitions with pointwise refinement; coarse conditional measures equal delta_x almost everywhere.
entries.fidelity: Exact after extending full-measure-domain partitions by a null atom. Lean's a.e. conclusion expresses the article's measure-one statement.

entries.label: thm:feng_entropy_as_limit
entries.exact_hypotheses: planar clause: every planar self-affine system (PlanarSystem), ergodic invariant probability measure μ on Σ, λ_2<λ_1, i ≤ 2. Projective clause: proximal box-like System with rotations, invariant probability measure ν carried by Σ_Z, ergodic or not, i ≤ 1 (rotations and proximality are not used).
entries.fidelity: both clauses at the article's scope (`feng_entropy_as_limit_general`); the box-like endpoints are specialisations through `System.toPlanar` (`feng_entropy_as_limit_boxLike_holds`). The library statements `System.feng_entropy_as_limit` and `System.feng_entropy_as_limit_bar` take FengInfoSum and FengInfoSumBar as hypotheses, which are theorems (`fengInfoSum_holds`, `fengInfoSumBar_holds`).
proof_deviations: Proof: the article quotes the limit from Feng. Lean proves Feng's identity (Lemma 4.6, first identity of (4.16)) along Feng's Lemmas 4.4 and 4.5 for every planar system with μ(Σ′)=1 (`PlanarSystem.infoSum_xi`, `infoSum_of_pullShift`) and for the projective system (`System.infoSum_xiBar`), and derives the limit from the proved Birkhoff theorem, as Feng does. μ(Σ′)=1 is the planar Oseledets theorem (`PlanarSystem.measure_SigmaPrime_compl_of_ergodic`), proved internally. Feng runs the induction (4.18) with the conditional-information chain rule; Lean multiplies conditional measures through his Lemma 4.5(3) and takes logarithms.

entries.label: thm:feng_entropy_kolmogorov_sinai
entries.exact_hypotheses: planar self-affine system (PlanarSystem: invertible linear parts of operator norm less than one), ergodic invariant probability measure on Σ, λ_2<λ_1: the article's hypotheses.
entries.fidelity: for every planar self-affine set and μ-almost every 𝐢 ∈ Σ′ the limit of -n⁻¹ log μ(𝒫_0^{n-1}(𝐢)) of the unconditional cylinder masses exists and equals h_0(μ, 𝐢) (`PlanarSystem.feng_entropy_kolmogorov_sinai_general`), with Σ′ the set of regular points of the Oseledets filtration of sec:lyapunov_exponents. The box-like endpoint `System.feng_entropy_kolmogorov_sinai` is its specialisation through `System.toPlanar` (`System.feng_entropy_kolmogorov_sinai_toPlanar`). h_0(μ)=h(μ) at the same scope is `PlanarSystem.dimEntropy_zero_eq_ksEntropy_of_ergodic`.
proof_deviations: Proof: Feng's (4.17) route through the Shannon-McMillan-Breiman theorem, proved internally by Breiman's argument (`shannonMcMillanBreiman`: Chung's maximal inequality, Lévy's theorem and Maker's theorem); ξ_0 is the past partition of Σ′ (`PlanarSystem.xi_zero_eq`). The input μ(Σ′)=1 is Oseledets' theorem for invertible planar cocycles, which the article cites and the library proves (`MatrixTuple.measure_regularSet_compl_of_ergodic`) from Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem (`kingman_ergodic`, from Birkhoff's theorem), the Furstenberg-Kesten limits along the backward products (`MatrixTuple.tendsto_log_norm_pastProd`, `MatrixTuple.tendsto_log_alpha₂_pastProd`) and the convergence of the slow directions (`MatrixTuple.exists_slow_fast_of_tendsto`). The Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy is the supremum over finite Borel partitions, attained at the time-zero partition (`ksEntropy_shift_eq_entropy`, the generator theorem). λ_2<λ_1 is needed for Σ′ and its measurability; the limit itself holds for every invariant measure with μ(Σ′)=1.

entries.label: thm:feng_entropy_zero
entries.exact_hypotheses: as for 3.5: planar clause for every planar self-affine system, ergodic μ, λ_2<λ_1, i ≤ 2; projective clause for invariant ν carried by Σ_Z, ergodic or not, i ≤ 1.
entries.fidelity: the article's stronger pointwise equivalence h_i(μ, 𝐢) = 0 ⟺ μ_𝐢^{ξ_i} = δ_𝐢 is proved at the article's scope (`feng_entropy_zero_general`), not merely Feng's global vanishing criterion; the scalar clause needs no ergodicity. The box-like endpoints are specialisations (`feng_entropy_zero_boxLike_holds`).
proof_deviations: Proof: as in the prose (`PlanarSystem.feng_entropy_zero_of_infoSum`): the invariant zero set of the conditional information, vanishing information along every forward iterate, the finite information-sum identity, mass one on every future cylinder, fixed past, and intersection to a Dirac measure; the converse through the pointwise limit of 3.5. Feng's identity is proved (`fengInfoSum_holds`, `fengInfoSumBar_holds`, `PlanarSystem.infoSum_xi`) and μ(Σ′)=1 is the planar Oseledets theorem, proved internally.

entries.label: thm:partitions_xi1
entries.exact_hypotheses: The four component endpoints require only a box-like System, a measure and membership in the corresponding orientation set; the Omega components additionally require lambda_2 < lambda_1. The combined wrapper has unused rotations, proximality, invariance and ergodicity binders.
entries.fidelity: All four identities and all four saturation inclusions are present. The combined wrapper adds proximality, which is absent from the explicit statement of this lemma, but the stronger component lemmas avoid that unnecessary assumption.

entries.label: thm:partition_tau_conj
entries.exact_hypotheses: The combined theorem takes rotations, proximality, invariance, ergodicity and a strict Lyapunov gap; as in 3.8 only the gap enters the actual identities, and underlying components remove the unused proximality binder. The identity holds for all natural n, stronger than n>=1.
entries.fidelity: Matches both orientation cases and the join with the future-cylinder partition; the unnecessary proximality binder should not be silently treated as part of the manuscript statement.

entries.label: thm:irred_eq_state
entries.exact_hypotheses: an irreducible tuple of invertible planar matrices (`TupleIrreducible`, det A_i != 0) and s>0 (`MatrixTuple.irred_eq_state_of_fengKaenmaki`, which takes FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium as a hypothesis for 0<s<2 only; Solution discharges it with `fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_holds`, `paper_3_10_25`). The irreducible box-like endpoint `System.irred_eq_state` takes an irreducible box-like System and the box-like predicates FengKaenmakiGibbs and FengKaenmakiUnique, which FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium implies and the library proves (`fengKaenmakiGibbs_holds`, `fengKaenmakiUnique_holds`, `paper_3_10_26`). Existence (`MatrixTuple.exists_isEquilibriumState`), the case s>=2 without irreducibility (`MatrixTuple.irred_eq_state_of_two_le`), ergodicity of a unique equilibrium state (`MatrixTuple.ergodic_of_unique`), existence of an ergodic equilibrium state for every s>=0, reducible or not (`MatrixTuple.exists_ergodic_isEquilibriumState`, tex 2217-2218), and the rescaling and two-sided reductions of the prose are proved without literature input. The endpoint for tuples with rotations (`System.irred_eq_state_of_withRotations`) takes a box-like System with rotations and s>0, and no literature premise.
entries.fidelity: the full statement at the article's scope, every irreducible tuple in GL_2(R)^N and every s>0: existence, uniqueness, ergodicity and the Gibbs bounds of the s-equilibrium state (`MatrixTuple.irred_eq_state_of_fengKaenmaki`; with no premise, `paper_3_10_25`), from `FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium` (BoxLike/LiteratureFengKaenmaki.lean), Feng-Kaenmaki, Proposition 1.2, in the form of the source, which the library proves (`fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_holds`). The irreducible box-like endpoint `System.irred_eq_state` is its specialisation through the box-like predicates (with no premise, `paper_3_10_26`). No literature premise is used. For box-like tuples with rotations, which need not be irreducible, the full statement holds for every s>0 with no literature premise (`System.irred_eq_state_of_withRotations`); the main line takes its Gibbs bounds through `EquilibriumGibbsStatement` (`equilibriumGibbs`) and its uniqueness through `System.unique_of_withRotations`.
proof_deviations: Proof: as in the prose: the norm potential for s<=1, the rescaled tuple A'_i = |det A_i|^((s-1)/(2-s)) A_i with exponent 2-s for 1<s<2 (`FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.svf`, `isEquilibriumState_iff_rescale`, `hasGibbsBounds_iff_rescale`), the reduction to the one-sided shift (`FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.twoSided`, `isNormEquilibriumPlus_map_eta_iff`), and the determinant Bernoulli calculation for s>=2, which Feng-Kaenmaki, Proposition 1.2, does not cover. Ergodicity follows from uniqueness (extreme points of the equilibrium states are ergodic, proved through the sub-affinity of entropy), which the source states as a remark after its (1.4).

Proof of Feng-Kaenmaki, Proposition 1.2 (BoxLike/QuasiMultiplicative/, `fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_holds`), along the architecture of Bowen's theorem: the norm of an irreducible tuple is quasi-multiplicative with connecting words of length at most one, by compactness of the unit sphere of the matrices, and invertibility is not needed (`MatrixTuple.normQuasiMultiplicative_of_irreducible`); for q>0 the periodic-orbit measures of ‖·‖^q satisfy uniform Gibbs bounds for every fixed word once their period is large, a weak-star limit point is an invariant Gibbs measure, and a Gibbs measure is ergodic by a quasi-Bernoulli lower bound (`normGibbsExistence`, `MatrixTuple.HasNormGibbs.ergodic`); for every q>=0 an invariant q-equilibrium state μ on Σ satisfies D_n(μ ‖ μ_q) <= log C on the cylinder partitions, so μ ≪ μ_q and μ = μ_q (`MatrixTuple.IsNormEquilibrium.eq_of_hasNormGibbs`); the one-sided statement follows through the natural extension (`exists_map_eta_eq`, `MatrixTuple.hasNormGibbsPlus_map_eta_iff`, `fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_of_normGibbsExistence`). The box-like predicates follow (`fengKaenmakiGibbs_holds`, `fengKaenmakiUnique_holds`).

Proof for tuples with rotations: for 0<s<2 the image μ_G = q_*μ₁ of Bowen's ergodic Gibbs measure μ₁ for f_{1,s} on Σ_Z has the Gibbs bounds with a constant K (`System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁`, `System.hasGibbsBounds_map_unCode`); for an invariant s-equilibrium state μ the equilibrium equation at level n and the lower Gibbs bound give the relative entropy bound D_n(μ ‖ μ_G) ≤ log K on the cylinder partitions (`IsEquilibriumState.blockRelEntropy_le`), hence μ ≪ μ_G (`absolutelyContinuous_of_blockRelEntropy_le`) and μ = μ_G, since μ_G is ergodic (`IsEquilibriumState.eq_map_unCode`); for s>=2 μ is the Bernoulli measure of 3.12. Uniqueness, ergodicity and the Gibbs bounds follow (`System.unique_of_withRotations`, `IsEquilibriumState.ergodic_of_withRotations`, `IsEquilibriumState.hasGibbsBounds_of_withRotations`).

literature_source_record.name: BoxLike.FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium
literature_source_record.citation: Feng-Kaenmaki, Equilibrium states of the pressure function for products of matrices, Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. 30 (2011), Proposition 1.2
literature_source_record.verification: Proposition 1.2 read in arXiv:1009.3129v1 (16 September 2010), p. 3, with its setting on pp. 1-2; the journal version was not consulted. The full source boundary record is the docstring of the definition.
literature_source_record.source_boundary: Source: F = R or C, d x d matrices irreducible over F^d (their Definition 1.1), the one-sided full shift, P(q) of their (1.1) with the standard matrix norm, M_*(mu) of (1.2), q-equilibrium states by (1.4); conclusion: for each q>0 a unique q-equilibrium state mu_q with the Gibbs property (1.6), and P'(q) = M_*(mu_q). Specialisation: F = R, d = 2, invertible matrices, the l2 operator norm (all norms give the same P, M_* and equilibrium states, and the Gibbs property with another constant), entropy entropyPlus of the generating partition, P and M_* as limUnder of convergent sequences (MatrixTuple.tendsto_normPressure, MatrixTuple.tendsto_normLyapPlus, tendsto_entropyPlus). Weaker than the source: no existence of mu_q (proved: MatrixTuple.exists_isEquilibriumState), the Gibbs property for n >= 1 only, no differentiability of P, no singular matrices (for which P(q) = -inf is possible and Real.log 0 = 0 would make a transcription false). Degenerate instances: the empty alphabet is not irreducible, so the statement is silent; for the one-letter tuple of the quarter turn the conclusion is proved (FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.degenerate_quarterTurn).
literature_source_record.reductions: FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.twoSided (the two-sided shift); FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.svf (the singular value potential for 0<s<2: q = s for s <= 1, the rescaled tuple A'_i = |det A_i|^((s-1)/(2-s)) A_i with q = 2-s for 1<s<2); FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.fengKaenmakiGibbs and .fengKaenmakiUnique (the box-like predicates FengKaenmakiGibbs and FengKaenmakiUnique).
literature_source_record.downstream_uses: MatrixTuple.irred_eq_state_of_fengKaenmaki (Proposition 3.10, thm:irred_eq_state, at the article's scope), which receives fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_holds in Solution (paper_3_10_25), and the reductions above; no headline result.
literature_source_record.exact_lean_declaration:
def FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium : Prop :=
  ∀ {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι]
    (A : ι → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ), (∀ i, (A i).det ≠ 0) → TupleIrreducible A →
    ∀ {q : ℝ}, 0 < q → ∀ (ν : Measure (ℕ → ι)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν],
    MeasurePreserving shiftPlus ν ν → MatrixTuple.IsNormEquilibriumPlus A q ν →
    MatrixTuple.HasNormGibbsPlus A q ν ∧
      ∀ (ν' : Measure (ℕ → ι)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν'], MeasurePreserving shiftPlus ν' ν' →
        MatrixTuple.IsNormEquilibriumPlus A q ν' → ν' = ν
literature_source_record.proof: The norm of an irreducible tuple is quasi-multiplicative with connecting words of length at most one, by compactness of the unit sphere of the matrices, without invertibility (MatrixTuple.normQuasiMultiplicative_of_irreducible); for q>0 Bowen's construction with periodic-orbit measures gives an invariant Gibbs measure of ‖·‖^q on the two-sided shift, ergodic by a quasi-Bernoulli lower bound (normGibbsExistence, MatrixTuple.NormQuasiMultiplicative.exists_ergodic_hasNormGibbs, MatrixTuple.HasNormGibbs.ergodic); for every q>=0 the equilibrium equation and the Gibbs bound give D_n(μ ‖ μ_q) <= log C on the cylinder partitions, so every invariant q-equilibrium state equals μ_q (MatrixTuple.IsNormEquilibrium.eq_of_hasNormGibbs, MatrixTuple.exists_ergodic_hasNormGibbs_forall_eq); the natural extension transfers this to the one-sided shift (exists_map_eta_eq, MatrixTuple.isNormEquilibriumPlus_map_eta_iff, MatrixTuple.hasNormGibbsPlus_map_eta_iff, fengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium_of_normGibbsExistence).

entries.label: thm:two-block-normalisation
entries.exact_hypotheses: a proximal System with rotations; s>0; an invariant s-equilibrium probability measure mu.
entries.fidelity: one endpoint (`System.two_block_normalisation`) assembles every conclusion: attractor equality; both matrix types; a proximal diagonal generator of the second iterate; preservation of strong separation, the strong open set condition and projective exponential separation; μ^(2) an invariant s-equilibrium state, the unique one, and ergodic; P(A², t) = 2P(A, t) for t>=0; h(μ^(2)) = 2h(μ) and both Lyapunov scalings; equality of the projected measures. The wrapper `System.two_block_normalisation_consequences` gives the affinity dimension, the Lyapunov dimension, the coordinate marginals and that grouping a Bernoulli measure gives a Bernoulli measure. The remark on invertible linear changes of coordinates (tex 2352-2353) is formalised in BoxLike/Planar/ChangeOfBasis.lean (`MatrixTuple.comparable_conj`, `PlanarSystem.ConjBy.*`).
proof_deviations: Proof: as in the prose; uniqueness and ergodicity come from Proposition 3.10 applied to A², which has rotations, with no literature premise (`System.unique_of_withRotations`, `IsEquilibriumState.ergodic_of_withRotations`); the proximal diagonal generator of A² squares the original one or comes from `hasProximalDiagonal_or_sq` (`Proximal.sq_hasProximalDiagonal`); the floor/subsequence argument gives projective separation.

entries.label: thm:bernoulli_equilibrium
entries.exact_hypotheses: Finite nonempty alphabet and box-like System, s>=2. Existing-measure uniqueness needs an invariant equilibrium probability measure, which itself implies the alphabet is nonempty. Proximality, rotations and separation are unnecessary.
entries.fidelity: Complete for the section's box-like setting, including s=2, the explicit normalised determinant weights, existence and uniqueness.

entries.label: thm:sigma_tau_omega_positive_eq_measure
entries.exact_hypotheses: System with rotations; 0<s<2; invariant ergodic equilibrium probability measure; hfk. Uniqueness is not used. No Morris-Shmerkin hypothesis or simple-spectrum assumption is required by this particular Lean endpoint, and proximality, a hypothesis of the manuscript, is not used. Proved input: BoxLike.EquilibriumGibbsStatement (`equilibriumGibbs`, the Gibbs bounds of Proposition 3.10 for tuples with rotations, proved in BoxLike/EquilibriumGibbs.lean); the library statements take it as a hypothesis and Solution discharges it.
entries.fidelity: Both positive-mass conclusions match, without the proximality of the manuscript. The Birkhoff display carries its almost-everywhere qualifier (tex 2462).
proof_deviations: Proof: as in the prose (`System.sigma_tau_omega_positive_eq_measure`, BoxLike/Aligned/SigmaTauOmega.lean, the form used by 4.6): the counting inequality summed along the orbit, and Birkhoff's theorem for the indicators of Σ^τ and of the anti-diagonal cylinders. The integrated one-step bound mu([i]) <= 2 mu(SigmaTau) from invariance (`System.sigma_tau_omega_positive`) is an alternative proof.

entries.label: thm:eq_state_is_sum
entries.exact_hypotheses: A box-like System with rotations and 0<s<2; an invariant probability measure μ with the Gibbs bounds of `thm:irred_eq_state`. EquilibriumGibbsStatement, a theorem of the library (`equilibriumGibbs`), passes from the manuscript's hypothesis "μ is the s-equilibrium state" to these Gibbs bounds, with no irreducibility and no proximal diagonal generator: every invariant s-equilibrium state is the image q_*μ₁ of the decomposition (`System.IsEquilibriumState.eq_map_unCode`). Pressure equalities need only a diagonal generator and 0<s<2. Integral identities and axis symmetry follow from a GibbsDecomposition witness.
entries.fidelity: The article quotes the proposition from Fraser-Jordan-Jurga (Lemma 1.3, Corollaries 1.5 and 1.6); the library proves it (`fraserJordanJurgaDecomposition_holds`): the ergodic s-Gibbs measures μ₁, μ₂ carried by Σ_Z, the four decompositions of μ, and λ_1(𝖠, μ) = \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₁), λ_2(𝖠, μ) = \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₂). The pressure identities P(𝖠, s) = P_Z(f_{1,s}) = P_Z(f_{2,s}) are `System.pressure_eq_pressureZ₁` and `System.pressure_eq_pressureZ₂`. Proximality and a proximal diagonal generator are not used. Every invariant measure with the Gibbs bounds equals the image of μ₁, so it is unique and ergodic, and the s-Gibbs measures of a decomposition are unique (`GibbsDecomposition.eq_mu₁`, `GibbsDecomposition.eq_mu₂`).
proof_deviations: Proof: Bowen's theorem (bowenGibbsExistence) gives the ergodic Gibbs measure μ₁ for f_{1,s} on the mixing Σ_Z (System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁), and μ₂ is its image under the exchange of the axes (System.isGibbs_potential₂_map_flipAxis); the image of μ₁ under forgetting the axis has the Gibbs bounds of φ^s, since each word has two lifts and φ^s(A_w) is the larger of the two exponentials (System.hasGibbsBounds_map_unCode); every invariant measure with the Gibbs bounds equals this ergodic measure (System.eq_of_hasGibbsBounds); the four decompositions follow from Σ_Z = τ(Σ) ⊔ ω(Σ) and the exchange of the two ranges; the Lyapunov identities follow from Birkhoff's theorem along the two lifts and the relative-entropy comparison \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₂) ≤ \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₁) (System.lyapunov_map_unCode_of_isGibbs).
